title: doer output
description: Canonical machine-readable output contract for the doer role. See agents/doer.md Step 3 (VERIFY checkpoint) and Branch and secrets rules (BLOCKED) for the prose contract this mirrors.

decision.description: REQUIRED when status is "NEEDS-DECISION", otherwise omit. The decision only a human operator can make before the named bead can go on. The orchestrator files it for an operator verbatim (never truncated), sets the bead aside for the rest of the run without re-dispatching it, and keeps working other ready beads. Use it only for a real choice between alternatives you cannot settle from the bead, its parent or the code -- not for a missing secret or an unmet prerequisite (BLOCKED), and not for an ordinary failure.

beadId.description: The one open bead id that cannot go on until the decision is made.

question.description: The full question, self-contained: what was found, why it blocks the bead, and what must be decided. An operator reads only this and the options.

options.description: At least two concrete alternatives, each with a short stable id (for example "a", "b") and its full text: what it means and what it costs.

recommendation.description: The option id you recommend, followed by why.

blockedIds.description: With status BLOCKED: the assigned bead ids you left open BECAUSE of the block -- not ids you merely did not reach (e.g. same-lane stop rule). The engine sets these beads, and every open bead depending on them, aside for the rest of the run. Optional -- omitted on a single-bead assignment it means that bead; omit or send [] with status VERIFY.

kb_captures.description: Durable knowledge this role verified during its run. The engine makes the kb_capture calls; the role only decides. Optional -- omit or send [] to capture nothing.

content.description: Full detail of the entry. REQUIRED -- kbCaptureSchema declares content as z.string().min(1), so a capture without it is rejected at the MCP boundary and persists nothing (apra-fleet-23c).

source_files.description: Files that make this claim checkable. At least one is REQUIRED -- SqliteProvider.capture() rejects an entry with no basis, because the freshness sweep can never stale it.

toolUse.description: How this run used the kb_* and code_* tools its role prompt expects (Step 0). Optional for backward compatibility, but expected: report "unavailable" or "not_needed" with a note rather than skipping the calls silently.

kb.description: used = kb_query was called (kb_session_prime alone is not used).

code.description: used = code_impact, code_context or code_graph was called.

note.description: Why a value is not "used": which tool was missing or failed, or why no lookup was needed.
